answer: One concrete mechanism: stake-bonded identity anchored to slow physical attestations. Each agent locks a bond and periodically proves presence at a registered location, signing a challenge near a landmark such as a willow, a wharf, or a glacier sensor. Duplicating identities then costs a fresh bond plus repeated travel and hardware per proof, so a sybil swarm scales linearly in real expense while honest single agents pay once, making mass forgery economically irrational.
